source_text: Hoc ergo ex nostro more adhuc solum exsequi cogitabam, id est ut a Traducianorum interpretationibus membra divinae Legis, quae subiacebant contumeliae, liberarem; quae erant scilicet divina, quod essent iusta monstrando.
pass_a_gloss: This therefore according to our custom I was still thinking to pursue alone, that is, that I might free from the interpretations of the Traduciani the members of the divine Law which were lying under insult; showing that they were divine, namely, because they were just.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Following my usual practice, this alone was what I still intended to do: to free those portions of the divine Law that were being insulted by the interpretations of the advocates of inherited sin. I would show that they were indeed divine by showing that they were just.

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: “Advocates of inherited sin” translates Julian's polemical label Traduciani, referring here to the transmission of sin by descent, not simply to a theory of the soul's origin.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
